What is one of your dislikes about reddit not currently being addressed by policies at Voat that you hope is addressed in the future?

I'm not convinced that there's much of anything that's significantly improved here over Reddit in terms of functionality, at least not yet. The karma system is tweaked a bit, but I think it's a flawed system to begin with and will ultimately have the same issues, though perhaps to a lesser extent. One of the big problems I have with reddit is people getting so concerned with maintaining a reputation through karma that they will adjust their opinions, whether consciously or otherwise, to fit the hivemind. Our accounts here still count up our internet points and put them next to our names, and upvotes are still given for agreement rather than simply quality of argument. Maybe it would be a good idea to not keep a tally next to the usernames. Numbers would be relevant in each individual thread for post order but not contribute to or detract from a user's reputation. This should at least limit the hivemind mentality a bit.

This reminds me of the palpable change when Atko implemented a vote ratio rule, where you can't downvoat if your up/down ratio is less than 1. There were some extremely douchy, downright toxic users that suddenly were less...toxic.

I think you're getting at a different thing though. The public display of the count is potentially an issue, but I think the numbers should matter none-the-less, even if they aren't shown.

There are a few things I don't like about reddit.

The downvoting system is dysfunctional.

A thread I started recently was on considering the idea of removing the anonymity of downvotes as a sort of a compromise between full unrestrained anonymous downvoting and removing downvotes entirely as others have suggested. The thread itself ended up a sort of poetic example of the problem with how downvotes are measured (and used) on this site and Reddit as well. In a short period of time after posting the thread it had received 4 upvotes. However, it'd also received 3 downvotes for a net score of +1. Consequently it ended up listed pages behind posts that were submitted weeks ago and received a total of 1 upvote. In other words a post that was clearly was generating discussion and interest was buried because 3 people thought downvote means "I disagree with this idea."
